ORAL ANSWERS TO QUESTIONS 
Support to Schemes for the poor 
*201. SHRI R. SHUNMUGASUNDARAM: Will the Minister of HOUSING AND 
N POVERTY ALLEVIATION be pleased to state: 
(a) the schemes under which the State Governments are being supported while providing 
rnative houses for the slum dwellers; and 
(b) whether there are Schemes executed by his Ministry where the dilapidated houses 
he poor are either repaired or rebuilt? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN 
J,RTY ALLEVIATION (KUMARI SELJA): (a) and (b) A Statement is laid on the "able 
of the Sabha. 
Statement 
(a) The Government of India supports State Governments for providing houses for 
 dwellers along with civic amenities in 63 identified cities under the scheme of Basic 
ices to the Urban Poor (BSUP) and in other cities/towns under the scheme of Integrated 
ung and Slum Development Programme (IHSDP) under the overall aegis of the 
awaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM). 
(b) Under BSUP and IHSDP guidelines, new construction as well as upgradation of 
houses for the urban poor are eligible for support from Government of India by way of 
\dditional Central Assistance. The admissible components under BSUP and IHSDP are 
given in the statement. 
Statement 
Admissible components under Basic Services to the Urban Poor (BSUP) 
• Integrated development slums, i.e., housing and development of infrastructure 
projects in the slums in the identified cities. 
• Projects involving development/improvement/maintenance of basic services to the 
urban poor. 
  •  Slum improvement and rehabilitation projects. 

2    Oral Answers [RAJYA SABHA] to Questions 
• Projects on water supply/sewerage/drainage, community toilets/baths, etc. 
• Housing at affordable costs for slum dwellers/urban poor/EWS/LIG categories. 
• Construction and improvements of drains/storm water drains. 
• Environmental improvement of slums and solid waste management. 
• Street lighting. 
• Civic amenities like community halls, child care centres etc. 
• Operation and maintenance of assets created under this component. 
• Convergence of health, education and social security schemes for the urban poor. 
Admissible components under Integrated Housing and Slum Development 
Programme (IHSDP) 
• Shelter including upgradation & construction of new houses. 
• Community toilets. 
• Physical amenities like water supply, storm water drains, community bath widenin* 
and paving of existing lanes, sewers, community latrines, street lights etc. 
• Community Infrastructure like community centres to be used for pre-schoc 
education, non-formal education, adult education, recreational activities etc. 
• Community Primary Health Care Centre Buildings can be. provided. 
• Social amenities like pre-school education, non-formal education, adult educatio  , 
maternity, child health and primary health care including immunization etc. 
• Model Demonstration Projects. 
• Sites and Services/houses at affordable costs for EWS & LIG categories. 
• Slum improvement and rehabilitation projects.

essential services to the city dwellers but they are not provided alternate sites and they are 
taken to some other area. The society is enco uraging slum dwellers because they provide 
cheap service to us. Sir, in Tamil Nadu, from 1979 onwards the Slum Clearance Board, 
which is functioning there, has built several multi-storeyed apartments for the slum dwellers 
and also provided alternative sites in different area. What is happening is that some of these 
houses are now in a dilapidated condition because there was no continuous maintenance of 
these newly built apartments. Therefore, I put my second question, part(b) of my question 
whether...

SHRI R. SHUNMUGASUNDARAM: First supplementary but relating to... 
MR. CHAIRMAN: One question, first supplementary. 
SHRI R. SHUNMUGASUNDARAM: This is the first supplementary relating to sew

MR. CHAIRMAN: All right. 

Oral Answers [13 MARCH 2008] to Questions   3 
SHRI R. SHUNMUGASUNDARAM: In the Second part of the question, the hon. 
Minister has answered that there are two schemes under which modernisation and upgradation 
are provided. Sir, but what is happening is that upgradation and modernisation are very wide 
terms. They do not cover the actual rebuilding of these houses, which are in a dilapidated 
condition because I understand that from the Tamil Nadu Slum Clearance Board, there were 
several demands made to the Central Governme nt for financial assistance for rebuilding 
these houses but money has not been provided so far. I would like to know what is being 
done in this regard. 
KUMARI SELJA: Sir, may I say that under the JNNURM we have two components 
the basic services for the urban poor for the large cities and for the smaller towns and cities 
we have IHSDP or the Integrated Housing and Slum Development Programme. Sir, as far as 
Tamil Nadu is concerned, Tamil Nadu is one of the States which is doing extremely well and 
for this year the sanction has been more than what was allocated for Tamil Nadu and it has 
been 116 per cent. We have under JNNURM sanctioned about 10 lakh houses till now and 
out of that one-tenth are from Tamil Nadu. Most of them are new dwelling units. We have 
received certain projects even for upgradation of the old houses numbering about 3000 only. 
Those projects have been received and they have been sanctioned. But for new dwelling 
units we have received most of the projects and about one lakh dwelling units have been 
sanctioned for Tamil Nadu. 
SHRI R. SHUNMUGASUNDARAM: Anyhow, Sir, but I understand that the demand 
from Tamil Nadu for rebuilding those houses is not conceded so far. So, my second 
supplementary is whether the Ministry is encouraging and giving assistance for houses for 
Other Backward Classes and the Most Backward Classes because in Tamil Nadu the Other 
Backward Classes and the Most Backward Classes are given alternative housing sites near 
urban area. I would like to know whether any assistance is given for that by the Ministry. 
KUMARI SELJA: This scheme is for slum dwellers and it is a demand driven project-
based scheme. Whatever projects are receive d from the State Governments, they are 
sanctioned after due appraisal by the Central Government and then, ACA is released. But 
most of the slum dwellers are from EWS and LIG categories. Most of them come from the 
Scheduled Castes, the Backward Classes and Other Backward Classes. But, we also have a 
certain provision that whereas all the slum dwellers will give about 12 per cent of the money 
as beneficiary contribution, but for the Scheduled Castes and Backward Classes, it will only 
be ten per cent. But it will be up to the State Government as to what projects they give us. It 
is not based on caste, in that sense, but again I would repeat most of the slum dwellers are 
from EWS and LIG; they came from these kinds of castes.

The Centrally Sponsored Sports Infrastru cture Schemes stand transferred to the 
state sector w.e.f. 1.4.2005 and as such, no fresh proposals were considered after 1.4.2005. 
As regards committed liabilities pertaining to projects sanctioned prior to this date, such 
proposals were considered upto 1.4.2007 subejct to fulfillment of the terms & conditions of 
the sanction order and availability of funds. 
In view of limited budget allocation for this purpose a significant portion of the 
committed liabilities in respect of a large number of sanctioned projects still remain 
nserviced, which includes 10 projects of Orissa, where the projects have either been 
completed or in the advance stage of completion. 
The Ministry has taken up the issue of funding the committee liabilities with the 
Planning Commission for favourable consideration. In the meanwhile, the Government has 
approved the proposal for implementing a nation wide Rural Sports Infrastructure 
Development Scheme under the title "Panchayat Yuva Krida and Khel Abhiyan (PYK.KA)", 
which aims at providing basic sports facilities at the panchayat level in a phased manner 
over a period of 10 years apart from promoting rural sports competitions at the block and 
district level. The Planning Commission has made allocation of Rs. 1500 crores for the 
implementation of PYKKA during the Xlth Five Year Plan. Similarly, they have also made 
token provision of Rs. 10 crores for 2008-2009 for undertaking a sports infrastructure 
scheme in urban areas.

*205. SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE: Will the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND 
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the country's National Security Advisor was asked to step in to resolve 
spectrum controversy and has met Department of Telecommunications, Telecom Rgulatory

THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY 
(SHRI A. RAJA): (a) to (d) A Group of Ministers (GoM) has been constituted for vacation 
of spectrum and raising resources for the purpose. In its first meeting (September, 2007), the 
GoM decided among others, to setup a committee under the national Security Adviser for 
speedy release/vacation of spectrum. The meeting of this committee scheduled in February 
2008 has been postponed. 
SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE: Sir, my first supplementary would be, what is the 
quantum of spectrum being released by the Defence for the teleco m operators and what 
steps is the DoT taking to ensure that the Defence communications needs are to be met after 
this release?

and for further discussion with the Department of Telecommunication and Department of 
Defence on this. For this, a Committee under the chairmanship of the National Security

scheduled in February, was postponed, and the meeting will take place in the near future.

with the Department of Defence. 
SHR1MATI SUPR1YA SULE: Sir, though the hon. Minister hasn't answered my

this case. By virtue of the Indian Telegraphs Act, the Ministry is the true owner of spectrum. 
Since time immemorial, and that too specifically, when the mobile telephone operation was 
not in existence, these spectrum were used by the Defence Ministry for various reasons, 
including, the Air Force, the Army and  the Navy. So, there must be a technical study between 
the two Ministries as to what quantum of sp ectrum is essentially needed for the Defence. 
Thereafter, they can decide how much spectrum can be allocated for civil purposes. Since it 
does require a technical study, the National Adviser was asked to have a look into that. That

supplementary, the hon. Member has made a good suggestion. Of course, as far as this 
suggestion is concerned, the Finance Ministry has already given its clearance. If there is a 
delay and if the DoT is intended to levy any reasonable charge, DoT is always at liberty. But, 
at this juncture, since the technical study is going on, we cannot say how much levy can be 
imposed on them.

t *208. SHRI LALIT KISHORE CHATURVEDI: t t DR. GYAN PRAKASH 
PILANIA: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Green India Campaign is being run by Government for 
implementing strategy to meet the climate change; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that the environment of forests has become unbalanced by 
uncontrolled afforestation of Prosopis Juliflora (Vilayati Babool) in Rajasthan, whose effect 
is reflecting as constant decline in wildlife and medicinal plants in the forests; and 
(d) whether there is any scheme to take help of voluntary agencies alongwith the forest 
officers working in States on afforestation under Green India Campaign? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND 
FORESTS (SHRI S. REGUPATHY): (a) to (d) A statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) and (b) The Ministry of Environment and Forests proposes to take up plantation 
over 6 million hectares of degraded forests of  the country in two Phases by utilizing the 
money collected under Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning 
Authority (CAMPA). This has been known as "Green India Programme". The money collected 
under CAMPA besides being used to partly finance the Green India Programme would be 
mainly used for site specific schemes approved for taking up compensatory afforestation, 
artificial regeneration (plantation), natural assisted regeneration, forest management, 
protection, infrastructure development, wildlife protection and management. These activities 
besides greening the country would also help in mitigating the adverse effects of climate 
change. 
(c) The State Government of Rajasthan has informed that Prosopis Juliflora had not 
been planted in Rajasthan during the last 10 years except on few refractory sites where other 
species would not come up. While Prosopis Juliflora is acting as an impenetrable barrier to 
biotic interference thereby contributing toward s conservation of biodiversity, there are a 
few areas where it has become menace to plants and wildlife. Therefore, its eradication in 
such areas has been taken up. 
(d) Under the proposed Green India Programme the implementation would be done 
through the mechanism of Joint Forest Management using the Forest Development Agencies 
(FDAs).

Status of Commonwealth Games, 2010 
202. DR. V1JAY MALLYA: Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS 
be pleased to state : 
(a) the status in respect of preparation of the 2010 Commonwealth Games to be held 
in our country; 
(b) the additional infrastructure that would be added for the games; and 
(c) the support given by Government of Indian teams in various disciplines in respect 
of preparation for the 2010 games? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS SHRI MANI SHANKAR 
AIYAR : (a) Government are conscious of the need to ensure proper planning and timely 
preparation for the Commonwealth Games, 2010 and to this end a number of institutional 
arrangements have been made. These include a Core Group of Ministers (GoM) under the co-
Chairmanship of the Minister for Human Recource Development and the Home Minister for 
coordinating the various works related to the conduct of the Games; an Apex Committee headed 
by the Minister for Yourth Affairs and Sports to oversee preparations; an Organizing Committee 
(OC) headed by the President, Indian Olympic Accociation for the conduct of the Games; and 
a Committee of Secretaries headed by Cabinet Secretary which is responsible for monitoring 
the implementation of the decisions of the GoM and taking decisions on other related matters. 
In additipn to these arrangements at the Central level, there is a sub-committee under the Chief 
Minister of Delhi to take decisions in respect of all matters pertaining to infrastructure and 
other preparations for the Games within the jurisdiction of the Government of NCT of Delhi. 
The Lt. Governor Delhi has been entrusted with the overall responsibility for matters coming 
under DDA and with specific reference to security, law and order. An Empowered Committee 
has been set up under the chairmanship of Chief Secretary, GNCTD, with representatives from 
all the agencies/authorities concerned to facilitate speedy cl earances in respect of Games-
related projects. Another Committee has been set up under Secretary, Ministry of Urban 
Development to facilitate clearances pertaining to the Delhi Urban Arts Commission DUAC). 
Keeping in view the need for developing adequate tourist accommodation in rediness for the 
large expected influx of visitors for the Commonwealth Games, an inter-Ministerial Task Force 
has been set up under the Ministry of Tourism (MoT) for monitoring and coordinating further 
action in this regard by all the agencies concerned. A Committee for expediting Central 
Government clearances in respect of hotels coming up in Uttar Pradesh has also been set up 
under the Chairmanship of Secretary, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sport. 
Locations for the various competitions/training venues and the International Broadcating 
Centre (IBC)/Main Press Centre (MPC) have been agreed among the stakeholders. All stakeholders 
have indicated specific time-lines with reference to key milestones, va., finalization of details 
designs and estimates, commencement of the tendering process, award of die work, commencement 
of the work, completion of the work; and handing over to OC. The work on all the major sports 
venue infrastructure projects has commenced and the venues are scheduled to be handed over to 
the OC by the end of 2009. The Ministry of Youth  Affairs & Sports had also set up a web-based 
monitoring system ot monitor and review project related to the Commonwealth Games. 
Government have approved project prooposals of the Sports Authority of India for an 
amount of Rs. 1000 crores (+10%) for the upgradation/creation of sports venue infrastructure;

upgradation of the tennis venue by the All India Tennis Association at a cost of Rs. 30 crores (+ 
15%); and an expenditure budget for the Organizing Committee on a revenue neutral basis of Rs. 
767 crores (+ 15%) for the 'Conduct of the Games'. The Expenditure Finance Committee have 
considered the proposal of the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) for about Rs. 765.00 crores 
for the International Zone etc. in the Games village (which is being developed in the Public 
Private Partnership Mode) and sports infrastructure at the Village/ other venues belonging to DDA. 
The Expenditure Finance Committee have also considered the proposal  amounting to Rs. 257.41 
crores of Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports for upgradation/creation of competition/training 
venues of CWG 2010 at the Delhi University, Jamia Millia Islamia University and Delhi Public 
School, RK Puram, New Delhi. 
The Planning Commission have approved the proposal of the Government of the NCT of 
Delhi for an amount of Rs. 770.00 crores. Planning Commission have also approved an amount 
of Rs. 210.00 crores to the Government of Maharashtra for sports infrastructure for the 
Commonwealth Youth Games, 2008 to be held in Pune, which is a sub-event of the main 
Commonwealth Games 2010. 
(b) For the Commonwealth Games, 2010, most of the Competition and Training Venues for 
the sports disciplines will be at the existing stadia, which are being upgraded/renovated for the 
purpose. Some new indoor halls and other facilities will be additionally created. The lists of the 
competition and training venues are given in statement I and statement II respectively.

extensive discussions have been held with all stakeholders and a programme for providing state 
of art training, foreign exposure, scientific backup, equipment etc. at an estimated cost of Rs. 
802.00 crore has been drawn up for the elite sportspersons who will represent India in the 
Commonwealth Games, 2010.

THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT (SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY): (a) to 
(e) Water-logging and flooding is an occasional phenomenon caused due to heavy rain fall 
which occurs in various cities from time to time. During the last three years, water-logging/ 
flooding has been observed in such cities as Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Bangalore, Hyderabad, 
Patna, Surat, Baroda, Guwahati. The main reasons for water-logging are high intensity of 
rain fall, inadequate drainage system, choking of drains due to lack of preventive maintenance 
and gathering of solid waste into the drains, conversion of low-lying areas into human 
settlements and improper planning of cities etc. 
Government of India have launched Jawahar Lai Nehru National Urban Renewal 
Mission (JNNURM) for reforms linked Central assistance to identified cities in the country. 
One of the admissible components of funding is storm water drainage system which would 
alleviate the problem of water-logging/flooding. The list of drainage projects so far approved 
by the Ministry of Urban Development is given the Statement (See below).

countries where the migrants are surviving in conditions unfit for human habitation, working 
at extremely low wages, suffering torture, exploitation, depression and death; and 
(b) the steps Government has taken in this regard and stop the illegal trading and 
arresting them? 
THE MINISTER OF OVERSEAS INDIAN AFFAIRS (SHRI VAYALAR RAVI): (a) 
The plight of the illegal worker in the host countries is par ticularly precarious because of 
the following reasons: 
(i) They get lower wages compared to those who emigrate legally. 
(ii) They have to face the vicissitudes of the labour market on a daily basis to find jobs 
and pay commission to the sponsors. 
(iii) The cannot negotiate fair conditions of work because of their illegal status. 
(iv) They cannot return home because of the poverty, debt burden and unemployment. 
(v) Due to their insecure position, they are often exploited, ill-treated and abused. 
(vi) Above all, the danger of getting caught and detained by Immigration always lurks. 
(b) On detection of illegal recruitment or emigration, action is taken by the Protector 
General of Emigrants against the recruiting agents and for foreign employees concerned. 
The illegal recruiters are prosecuted with the help of the State Police. During 2007 registration 
certificates of 8 recruiting agents were cancelled. At the moment 336 foreign employees are 
on the blacklist. During 2007 we received 41 complaints of illegal recruitment. Prosecution 
sanctions were issued in 7 cases based on police reports. 
The Indian Mission plays an important role in mitigating the problems of the victims 
of illegal migration. Proceedings in the labour courts are initiated against the employer if the 
conciliation efforts fail. If it becomes necessary the Indian Mission provides humanitarian 
support to the distressed worker and arranges his repatriation. The Indian community lends 
a helping hand to the Missions in carrying out these tasks. The Missions take measures for 
maximizing benefits to such workers under Amnesty schemes of the destination countries. 
The Ministry, recognizing the need for proactive preventive measures to stop illegal 
migration and strengthen the protection and welfare of emigrants by appropriate interventions 
at various levels, has initiated action at three levels—national, bilateral and multilateral—to 
make emigration of workers from India an orderly and humane economic activity for the 
benefit of all stakeholders. 
At the national level the Ministry is pursuing a policy of actively discouraging illegal 
migration and facilitating legal/managed migration. To this end we have taken several steps. 
We are in the process of amending the Emig ration Act to create appropriate provisions to 
support promotion and facilitation of legal migration, provide for more stringent penalties 
for offences, creating penal provision against the offence of human smuggling, increasing 
the penalty for illegal migration and strengthening the regulation of recruiting agents. The 

40    Written Answers to [RAJYA SABHA] Starred Questions 
Ministry has set up an Overseas Workers' Resource Centre with a 12/7 helpline to provide 
an avenue to potential emigrants for accessing information on legal migration channels. To 
actively build awareness amongst potential emigrants about the risks involved in illegal 
migration and the precautions to be taken during the migration process a multimedia publicity 
campaign has been launched. 
The Ministry is undertaking emigration reforms to make the emigration process simple, 
transparent and efficient. We have done away with the requirement of exit clearance for 
those travelling on visit visa to save non-emigrants from undue inconvenience, harassment 
and expenditure. This is also aimed at curbing Corruption in the emigration system. The 
Ministry has libealized the criteria for issue of passports to save educated people from undue 
inconvenience, harassment and expenditure. The Ministry is committed to apply the 
emigration controls only in respect of vulnerable sections of emigrants in order to ensure 
their protection and welfare. To protect women emigrants from exploitation, their emigration 
on ECR passport to ECR countries is allowed only above the age of 30 years and their 
labour contracts must be attested by the Indian Missions concerned. The emigration clearance 
system has been computerized recently. A comprehensive e-governance project will be 
implemented to transform the emigration system into a technology managed process, linking 
all stakeholdes for online verification/validation of information to prevent malpractices like 
emigration on forged documents. The regulatory system for recruting agents is being made 
more stringent. 
At the bilateral level the Ministry has been actively pursuing the signing of formal 
MoUs with the major labour receiving countries not only to secure their commitment towards 
the protection and welfare of Indian workers but also aimed at streamlining the deployment 
procedures and removing the loopholes in the system. In December 2006 the Government 
signed an MoU with the UAE and in April 2007 with Kuwait. In November 2007 an additional 
Ptotocol with Quatar was signed to update the 1985 Agreement. MoU are being finalized 
Malaysia and Oman. MoU are also being pursued with Bahrain and Yemen. Further, to 
supplement the Agreement the Government of India had signed with the Government of 
Tordanm 1988, it is proposed to Sign an Additional Protocol to the 1988 Agreement. Efforts 
are on to persuade the KSA to negotiate an MoU on labour with India. 
At the multilateral level we have signed an MoU with the IOM for implementing the 
Asia-EU project for Regional Dialogue and Program for facilitating legal migration between 
Asia and the EU countries. The project is already under implementation and will give us an 
opportunity for capacity building towards migration management and develop overseas 
employment market in the strategically important European countries and upgrade the Indian 
workers in the wage chain.

Implementation of Yamuna Action Plan 
♦217.     SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: Will 
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) the progress so far made in the implementation of the Yamuna Action Plan and the 
expenditure incurred thereon so far; 
(b) whether the Plan has so far failed in its object; and 
(c) if so, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND 
FORESTS (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) to (c) The Government of India has 
undertaken Yamuna Action Plan (YAP) for abatement of pollution of river Yamuna with the 
assistance from Japan Bank for International Cooperation. Government of Japan in a phased 
manner. YAP Phase-I was launcherd in 1993 with the completion period upto the year 2000. 
However, this phase was extended upto 2003 owing to inclusion of additional works on the 
directions of Hon'ble Supreme Court as well as by the Government of India . The second 
phase of YAP was started in December 2004 with the completion period of 5 years. 
A total of 269 pollution abatement works pertaining to interception and diversion of 
sewage, installation of Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs), Low Cost Sanitation, Crematoria, 
River Front Development, Public Participation and Awareness among others, were taken up 
in YAP Phase-I at a cost of Rs. 682 crore in 21 towns in the three States of U.P., Haryana and 
Delhi. A total of 38 STPs having a treatment capacity of 753.25 million litres per day (mid) 
have been created under this phase. 
YAP Phase-II was formulated to take up other pollution abatement works of the river 
Yamuna, as prioritized by the States. This phase includes, (i) installation/rehabilitation of 
STPs and rehabilitation/replacement of trunk sewers in Delhi, (ii) installation of STPs, laying 
of sewer lines and rising mains in Agra, Uttar Pradesh and , (iii) laying of sewer in six towns 

42    Written Answers to [RAJYA SABHA] Starred Questions 
of Haryana. The estimated cost of this phase is Rs. 624 crores . An amount of Rs. 61.14 
crores has been released to the State Governments for completion of 20 schemes sanctioned 
under this Plan so far. These schemes are under various stages of progress. In addition to the 
above, the Government of the NCT of Delhi has also taken up large scale sewerage, non-
sewerage and sewage treatment works out of its own Plan funds. 
While the water quality of river Yamuna is within the prescribed limits in the State of 
Haryana, it has not shown the desired improvement in Delhi and some parts of U.P. because 
of phenomenal increase of population upstream of the river and lack of availability of fresh 
water for ensuring minimum flow in the river.

*220. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA TAIMUR: 
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: 
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that during December 2007 about 200 Maoist ultras from Nepal 
staked their claim on a stretch of no-man's-land' in Uttarakhand and hoisted their red flag in a 
town in border district of Champavat; 
(b) if so, whether the border-pillars are not existing in this area; and

demarcate the border so that such incidents do not recur and border-pillars are duly fixed to identify 
Indo-Nepalese border? 
THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS (SHRI PRANAB MUKHERJEE): (a) to (c) 
The India-Nepal boundary has been primarily established on the basis of the Treaty of Sugauli 
of 1815 and the subsequent Memorandum of 1816 as amended and confirmed by the Treaty of 
1860. The open border with Nepal extends over an estimated length of 1900 kilometres. 
Strip map surveys of 99% of the border and identification of 97.7% of the boundary on the 
ground has been completed. Boundary strip maps have been printed for all segments of the 
boundry that have been identified and have also been signed at the level of the Joint Technical 
Committee (JTC) on boundary matters. It has been further decided to set up an inter-Government 
Boundary Working Group as successor to the JTC, to inter alia delineate boundary line in the 
remaining sectors, and undertake inspection, construction, maintenance, and repair of boundary 
pillars. 
On December 25,2007, activists of the Young Communist League (YCL) of Nepal, an 
organisation affiliated to the Communist Party of Nepal (Maoist), attempted to crossover from 
Kanchanpur district of Nepal into the Indian territory near Banbasa in Champawat district of 
Uttarakhand, where border pillar positions have been jointly agreed to. The Indian border 
guarding forces, already on alert, took appropriate action to repulse the YCL activists.

Fire incidents in coal mines 
 t 1406. SHRI JA1 PARKASH AGGARWAL: Will the PRIME MINISTER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) thejieasons for fire incidents taking place in the coal mines and the remedial steps 
taken by Government in this regard; 
(b) the amount spent by Government till date on the security of coal mines and factories 
situated in the various States during the last two years; and 
(c) the measures taken for improving anti-fire systems of coal mines and factories? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL (DR. DASARI 
NARAYAN RAO): (a) The basic cause of coal mine fire is self-heating or auto-oxidajion of 
coal that starts as soon as it is exposed to the air in the course of mining operations. When 
the heat generated by the reaction of oxidation of coal is not dissipated at an adequate rate 
rise in temperature occurs. This rise in te mperature leads to acceleration in the rate of 
oxidation, which can ultimately lead to an outbreak of fire. This is termed as spontaneous 
heating, which depends on the intrinsic char acteristics of coal and other extrinsic causes 
encountered in the course of mining operations, which may facilitate or retard initiation of 
mine fire. The intrinsic properties are like chemical composition of coal (presence of certain 
macerals e.g. vitrinite etc.), moisture content, volatile matter, presence of pyrites and other 
geological factors. The extrinsic causes are like method of mining (such as depillaring with 
caving etc.), ventilation, presence of external combustible materials, un-scientific mining in 
past etc. Some coal seams, especially in Raniganj, Jharia, South Karanpura coalfields, are 
more susceptible to spontaneous heating which increases the possibility of mine fire. 
As per Coal Mine Regulation (CMR) 1957(116A, 117,118,118A&' 119) the remedial 
precautionary steps are being taken by CIL against spontaneous heating and accidental fires 
in mines. The precautionary steps against spontaneous heating and accidental fires so taken 
by Coal India Limited (CIL) are being monitored from time to time by law enforcing agency 
of Government of India i.e. Director General of Mine Safety (DGMS).

1414. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will the Minister of COMMUNICATION AND 
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd. had undertaken evaluation of work performance 
of its many SC/ST employees and found 75 per cent of them as unfit/marginal as a prelude

representation for SC/ST categories; and

SC/ST employees even after disinvestments, with the Centre still being a majority stake holder?

INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a) No, the Company is not 
resorting to performance evaluation of the SC/ST employees of VSNL as prelude to 
retrenchment. The Company has a System of carrying out an annual performance review for 
all its employees and this is similar to the process adopted by many organizations. 
The performance is evaluated against specific objectives/job carried out and not on 
the basis of caste/creed/religion etc. The statement that 75% of the people have been rated as 
unfit/marginal is incorrect. 
(b) The employment of new employees is done as per the needs of the business and the 
same is, on merits and qualifications after a thorough and objective selection process. 
(c) There is no undertaking given by VSNL to the Centre at the time of disinvestment 
to protect SC/ST employees on roll at that time. However, at the time of disinvestment, an 
assurance was given in writing by Panatone (the Strategic Partner), that no employee in 
VSNL would be retrenched for a period of two years instead of one year as provided in the 
Shareholders Agreement, and that the present salary, wages and prerequisites would not be 
altered and no adverse change would be made in the retirement benefits which the employees 
on the roll of VSNL were eligible. These assurances have been fulfilled and complied with.

and holds only 26.12% stake.

River Ganga becoming reservoir of E. Coli 
1426. DR. (SHRIMATI) NAJMA A. HEPTULLA: Will the PRIME MINISTER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government is aware that as per new scientific evidence Ganga river has 
become reservoir of virulent forms of the bacteria. Escherichia coli known to cause ailments 
ranging from mild intestinal disease to severe kidney complications; 
(b) whether Government is also aware that Ganga is most polluted at Kanpur, Varanasi 
and Haridwar; 
(c) whether Government is also aware that Gangajal kills 250 a year; and 
(d) if so, what Government has done to clean the holy river from pollutants? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND 
FORESTS(SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) and (b) Indian Council of Medical 
Research and National Institute of Communicable Diseases under the Ministry of Health & 
Family Welfare. Government of India, are reportedly neither aware nor have conducted any 
study or survey regarding the Ganga river becoming a reservoir of virulent forms of bacteria, 
Escherichia coli. 
The monitoring of water quality of river Ganga under the Ganga Action Plan indicates 
that the water quality of river is not complying with the desired standards in stretches along 
the towns of Kanpur and Varanasi, but meeting with the norms in its stretch along the Haridwar

town. The levels of Fecal Coligorms (bacterial indicator for health concerns) are also reported 
to be exceeding the maximum permissible limit of 2500 MPN (Most Probable Number) per 
100 milliliter at many of the monitoring stations along river Ganga except in upstream locations 
of Haridwar. 
(c) No report is available with the Government in this regard. 
(d) The Ministry, since 1985, has been implementing the Ganga Action Plan (GAP) 
for pollution abatement activities in the identified polluted stretches of river Ganga. Under 
this Plan a total sewage treatment capacity of 1765.34 million litres per day has been created 
so far for Ganga and its major tributaries.  Despite phenomenal increase in the urban 
population along the banks of the river leading to increased pollution loads, the water quality 
of river Ganga has shown discernible improvement in terms of organic pollution at major 
locations, over the pre-Action Plan water quality. 
Problem of e-waste 
1427. SHRIB. J. PANDA: 
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government is aware that Indi a is reeling under mounds of e-waste 
generated due to worn-out electronic goods like computers, cell phones and televisions etc., 
(b) whether Government is also aware that in the European Union countries it is 
mandatory for the manufacturing companies to recycle the e-waste, but India is turning a 
blind eye to the accumulation of the above harmful e-waste; and 
(c) if so, the action plan of Government to address this problem? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND 
FORESTS (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) Based on a survey conducted under the 
guidance of the Central Pollution Conrol Board (CPCB) it has been estimated that about 
1,46,000 tons of Waste from Electrical and Electronic Equipment [WEEE] is generated 
annually in the country. 
(b) and (c) According to WEEE Directives of the European Union (EU), waste electrical 
or electronic equipments which include all components consumables etc. after use are to be 
disposed off as per the provisions of their National Law enforced. Further, EU directives 
focus on the restriction of the use of certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic 
equipments which has come into force with effect from January, 2007. These directives 
provide for the reduction and el imination of hazardous substa nces used in electrical and 
electronic equipments. 
The Ministry of Environment and Forests have notified the Hazardous Waste 
(Management and Handling) Rules, 1989 as amended in 2003 which regulate the generation, 
collection, storage, treatment, disposal as well as export and import of hazardous wastes, 
which include e-waste. The processes generating hazardous wastes are listed in Schedule 1 
of these rules. The residues and wastes generated from the operations in electronic industry 
are already considered as hazardous wastes and are included at Sl.No. 31 of Schedule 1 of 
these rules. Further, the import and export of e-waste is also regulated under Schedule 3 of 

74    Written Answers to [RAJYA SABHA] Unstarred Questions 
these rules. As per the provisions of these rules, the import of e-waste is regulated under 
Schedule 3 of these rules wherein Electrical and Electronic Assemblies are covered under 
category A 1180 in the list A and B 1110 in list B of the Schedule 3. The import of such waste 
is permitted only for direct reuse and not for recycling of final disposal. 
The Ministry of Environment and Forests had also constituted a Task Force to finalise

The steps taken by the Government for covering tiger and other wild animals 
Legal steps 
1. Amendment of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 for providing enabling 
provisions for constitution of the National Tiger Conservation Authority and the 
Tiger and Other Endangered Species Crime Control Bureau.The punishment in 
cases of offence within a tiger reserve has been enhanced. The Act also provides 
for forfeiture of any equipment, vehicle or weapon that has been used for committing 
any wild life offence. 
Administrative steps 
2. Strengthening of antipoaching activities, including special strategy for monsoon 
patrolling, by providing funding support to Reserve States, as proposed by them, 
for deployment of antipoaching squades involving ex-army personnel/homeguards, 
apart from workforce comprising of local people, in addition to strengthening of 
communication/wireless facilities. 
3. 100% Central Assistance provided to 17 Tiger Reserves as an additionality fo.-
deployment of Tiger Protection Force, comprising of ex-army personnel and local 
workforce. 
4. Constitution of the National Tiger Conservation Authority with effect from 
4.09.2006,for strengthening tiger conservation by, inter-alia, ensuring normative 
standards in tiger reserve management, preparation of reserve specific tiger 
conservation plan, laying down annual/audit report Parliament, constituting State 
level Steering Committee under the Chairmanship of Chief Ministers and 
establishment of Tiger Conservation Foundation. 
5. Constitution of a multidisciplinary Tiger and Other Endangered Species Crime 
Control Bureau (Wildlife Crime Control Bureau) with effect from 6.6.2007 
comprising of officers from Police, Forest, Customs and other enforcement agencies 
to effectively control illegal trade in wildlife. 
6. Approval accorded for declaring eight new Tiger Reserves.

7. The revised Project Tiger guidelines have  been issued to Stat es for strengthening 
tiger conservation, which apart from ongoing activities, inter-alia, including funding 
support to States for enhanced relocation/rehabilitation package for people living 
in core or critical tiger habitats (from Rs. 1 lakh/family to Rs. 10 lakh/family), 
rehabilitation/resettlement of communities involved in traditional hunting and 
mainstreaming livlihood and wildlife concerns in forests outside tiger reserves and 
fostering corridor conservation through restorative strategy to arrest habitat 
fragmentation.

and assessment of habitat status) has been evolved and mainstreamed. The findings 
of this estimation/assessment are benchmarks for future tiger conservation strategy.

conservation inputs through tiger reserve States. 
Financial steps

Schemes, viz. Project Tiger and Development of National Parks and Sanctuaries 
for enhancing the capacity and infrastructure of the States for providing effective 
protection to wild animals. 
International Cooperation 
12. India has Memorandum of Understanding with Nepal on controlling trans-boundary 
illegal trade in wildlife and conservation, apart from a protocol on tiger conservation 
with China.

international issues related to tiger conservation.

from 3rd to 15th June, 2007 at The Hague, India introduced a resolution along with 
China, Nepal and the Russian Federation, with directions to Parties with operations 
"breeding tigers on a commercial scale, for restricting such captive populations to a

decision with minor amendments. Further, India made an intervention appealing to 
China to phase out tiger farming and eliminate stockpiles of Asian big cats body 
parts and derivatives. The importance of continuing the ban on trade of body parts 
of tigers was emphasized.

Action plan for cleaning the rivers 
t l439. SHRIMATI SUSHMA SWARAJ: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that an action plan has been formulated to clean and to make the 
rivers of the country pollution free; 
(b) if so, the details of the rivers included in this plan; and 
(c) whether any time limit has been fixed to clean up these rivers? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND 
FORESTS (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) and (c) Under the Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme of National River Conservation Plan (NRCP), pollution abatement works are 
implemented to improve the water quality in the identified polluted stretches of major rivers. 
These works include interception and diversion of raw sewage flowing into the rivers, setting 
up of Sewage Treatment Plants for treating the diverted sewage, creation of low cost sanitation 
facilities, setting up of electric/improved wood crematoria and River Front Development 
among others. The Works are implemented through Implementing Agencies nominated by 
the State Governments for the purpose. Presently, NRCP covers pollution abatement works 
in 164 towns along polluted stretches of 35 rivers spread over 20 States at an approved cost 
of Rs. 4863.75 crores. The details of the rivers and the States covered under the Plan are 
given in Statement {See below). 
Conservation of rivers is a dynamic activity with the ever increasing pollution load 
due to rapid urbanization and increase in population. Review of the strategies of 
conservation policy and identification of additional towns and rivers is a continuous 
process. Due to continuous increase in th e population of the towns located along the 
banks of the rivers resulting in increased pollution load, and gap in the availability of 
financial resources to take up works commensu rate with the requirements, there is likely 
to be persistent divergence between the tackled pollution load and the actual pollution 
load.

1441. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to

controlled would adversely impact our environment and agricultural productivity;

developed countries to contain the adverse impact of climate change;

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT AND 
FORESTS (SHRI NAMO NARAIN MEENA): (a) The climate change has emerged as a 
global environmental challenge and is projected to adversely impact various aspects.

term issue. The greenhouse gases have a long retention time in the atmosphere. Impact of these 
greenhouse gases will continue to manifest throughout 21 st century.

Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and has set up the National Clean 
Development Mechanism Authority to accord Host Country A pprovals to e ligible Clean 
Development Mechanism (CDM) projects as per the requirements of Marrakesh Accords.

UNFCCC, yet, a sustainable development path is being followed in India by a range of policies 
and programmes to mitigate climate change. In dia is a partner to the new Asia Pacific 
Partnership on Clean Development and Climate which consists of both developed and developing 
countries—Australia, Canada, China, Japan, South Korea and the USA besides India. India has also 
been impressing upon developed countries to transfer environmentally

The steps taken by the Government to protect wild animals including tiger: 
Legal steps 
1. Amendment of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 for providing enabling

cases of offence within a tiger reserve has been enhanced. The Act also provides

workforce.

standards in tiger reserve management, preparation of reserve specific tiger 
conservation plan, laying down annual/audit report before Parliament, constituting 
State level Steering Committees under the Chairmanship of Chief Ministers and 
establishment of Tiger Conservation Foundation. 
5. Constitution of a multidisciplinary Tiger and Other Endangered Species Crime 
Control Bureau (Wildlife Crime Control Bureau) with effect from 6.6.2007 
comprising of officers from Police, Forest, Customs and other enforcement agencies 
to effectively control illegal trade in wildlife.

tiger conservation, which apart from ongoing activities, inter alia, include funding 
support to States for enhanced village relocation/rehabilitation package for people

family rehabilitation/resettlement of communities involved in traditional hunting 
and mainstreaming livelihood and wildlife concerns in forests outside tiger reserves 
and fostering corridor conservation through restorative strategy to arrest habitat 
fragmentation.

Statement 
Scheme for Giving Legal/Financial Assistance to Women Deserted by their Overseas 
Indian Spouses 
I. Objective: 
The objective of the scheme is to provide some financial assistance to needy women 
iff distress who have been  deserted by their overseas Indian spouses for obtaining counseling 
and legal services. The term "Overseas Indian" would include NRIs and foreign citizens of 
Indian origtn.The counseling and legal services would be provided through credible Indian 

Written Answers to [13 MARCH 2008] Unstayed Questions    127 
Women's Organizations/Indian Community Associations and NGOs identified for providing 
such services and empanelled with the Indian Missions in the USA, the UK, Canada, 
Australia, New Zealand and the Gulf. The scheme is a welfare measures to support women 
of Indian origin in distress, through the mobilization of the local Indian community in the 
endeavor and with some financial assistance from the Government. 
II. Scope of and Eligibility for the Scheme: 
The scheme would be available to the women who have been deserted by their overseas 
Indian spouses or are facing divorce proceedings in a foreign country subject to the following 
conditions:(i) The woman is an Indian passport holder. 
(ii) The marriage of the woman has been solemnized in India. 
(iii) The women is deserted in I ndia or after reaching abroad with five years of the 
marriage. 
(iv) Divorce proceedings are initiated within five years of the marriage by her overseas 
Indian spouse. 
(v) An ex-parte divorce has been obtained by the overseas Indian spouse within 
10 years of marriage and a case for maintenance and alimony is to be filed. 
(vi) The scheme would not be available to a woman facing criminal charges or having 
a criminal case decided against her. 
(vii) The domicile of the woman seeking relief under the scheme is not relevant for 
allowing the benefit. The woman may be domiciled in the country of her overseas 
Indian spouse or in India at the time of making the application. 
(viii) Preference may be given to applicants on the basis of financial needs. 
(ix) Assistance will be limited to meeting in itial cost and incidental charges for 
documentation and filing of the case by the Indian women's organization/NGO on 
the woman's behalf. 
(x) The assistance will be limited to US $ 1000 per case and will be released to the 
Indian community organizations/NGO concerned to enable to take  steps to assist 
the woman in documentation and preparatory work for filing the case. 
(xi) The women's organization/NGO will make efforts to enlist community advocates, 
preferably women advocates, to extend further legal assistance/appearance in court 
etc. on a pro-bono basis. 
III. Pattern of Assistance 
Under the scheme Indian Missions in the countries concerned would empanel cerebile 
Indian Women's Organizations/ Indian Community Associations/NGOs and their member 
advocates, preferably women, to provide legalaid to the victims in distress and whose names 
have been approved by the Ministry of Overseas Indian Affairs. The applications for providing 
legal aid received by the Missions would be examined by an officer designated by the Head 
of the Mission on case-to-case basis and approved by Head of Mission/Deputy Chief of the 
Mission.

The applications received in the Ministry of Overseas Indian Affairs will be examined 
by an internal committee consisting of a legal advisor and an officer of the rank of Director/ 
Deputy Secretary and approved by Secretary. Thereafter, the Ministry will recommend the 
case of Mission concerned to provide legal aid support. The applicant would also be informed 
to approach the Mission concerned in this regard.

1486. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN: Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether Gram Sabha has a substantial part in the implementation of Forest Rights 
Act (FRA); 
(b) if so, the details including processes initiated by Gram Sabha for implementation 
of FRA as on today, State-wise, category-wise; 
(c) if so, the details of claims filed in pres cribed format and number of such claims 
collected and forwarded by Gram Sabha as on today, State-wise, category-wise; 
(d) if so, whether there is any delay in convening meeting of Gram Sabha for initiating 
various processes in the implementation of Forest Rights Act; and 
(e) if so, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF PANCHAYATI RAJ (SHRI MANI SHANKAR AIYAR): (a) 
Yes, Sir. As per the provisions of the Sc heduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest 
Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (2 of 2007), the Gram Sabha is the 
competent authority for initiating the process of determining the nature and extent of forest 
rights to be recognized and vested, which are to be scrutinized by the Sub-Divisional Level 
Committee, after which the District Level Committee will approve the claims and record of 
forest rights. Section 6 (1) of the Forest Rights Act states that "the Gram Sabha shall be the 
authority to initiate the process for determining the nature and extent of individual or 
community forest rights or both that may be given to the forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes 
and other traditional forest dwellers within the local limits of its jurisdiction under this Act 
by receiving claims , consolidating and verifying them and preparing a map delineating the 
area of each recommended claim in such manner as may be prescribed for exercise of such 
rights and the Gram Shaba shall, then, pass a resolution to that effect and thereafter forward 
a copy of the same to the Sub-Divisional Level Committee." 
Rule 3 of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of 
Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (2 of 2007) states that "the Gram Sabhas shall be convened by the 
Gram Panchayat and in its first meeting it shall elect from amongst its members, a committee 
of not less than ten but not exceeding fiftee n persons as members of the Forest Rights 
Committee, wherein at least one-third members shall be the Scheduled Tribes: provided that 
not less than one-third of such members shall be women, provided further that where there 
are no Scheduled Tribes, at least one-third of such members shall be women". 
Rule 4 lays down functions of the Gram Sabha and states that "the Gram Sabha shall 
(a) initiate the process of determining the nature and extent of forest rights, receive and hear 
the claims relating thereto; (b) prepare a list of claimants of forests rights and maintain a 
register containing such details of claimant s and their claims as the Central Government 
may by order determine; (c) pass a resolution on claims on forest rights after giving reasonable 
opportunity to interested persons and authorities concerned and forward the same to the 
Sub-Divisional Level Committee, (d) consider resettlement packages under clause (e) of 
sub-sec*'on (2) of Section 4 of the act and pass appropriate resolutions; and (e) constitute 
Committees for the protection of wildlife, forest and biodiversity, from amongst its members, 
in order to carry out the provisions of section 5 of the act". 

Written Answers to [13 MARCH 2008] Unstarred Questions    135 
Rule 11 details the procedure for filing, determination and verification of claims by 
the Gram Sabha. The rule states that "the Gram Sabhas shall (a) call for claims and authorize 
the Forest, Rights Committee to accept the claims in the Form, as provided in Annexure-I of 
these rules and such claims shall be made within a period of three months from the date of 
such calling of claims along with at least two of the evidences mentioned in rule 13, shall be 
made within a period of three months, provided that the Gram sabha may if consider necessary, 
extend such period of three months after recording the reasons thereof in writing; (b) fix a 
date for initiating the process of determination of its community forest resource and intimate 
the same to the adjoining Gram Sabhas where there are substantial overlaps, and the Sub-
Divisional Level Committee." 
(b) to (e) After operationalization of the Act and notification of the Rules, the Ministry 
of Tribal Affairs has written to all State/UT Governments on 11.1.2008 to constitute various 
Committees under the Act Immediately and also initiate necessary action for recognition 
and vesting of the forest rights in the forest dwelling Scheduled Tribes and other traditional 
forest dwellers under the Act. The Ministry  of Panchayati Raj has also written to the 
States/UTson 15.2.2008 suggesting that the states may organize Gram Sabhas on 28.2.2008 
during which the provisions of the Act and th e Rules and the roles and responsibilities of

Study of developmental activities 
1495. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARATAIMUR: 
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government has made any in-depth study of the developmental activities 
and their visible imprint for equal distribution of benefits across the economic ladder, both 
during the period of mixed economy till eighties, and after "liberalization and massive dose 
of subsidies" from nineties onwards; and 
(b) if so, whether the extant policies and programmes being followed, both at the 
Central and States, are adequate for moving towards a competitive economy in the global 
scenario not only to sustain a vibrant and liberal polity, but India becoming a developed 
Nation by 2020? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING (SHRI M.V. 
RAJ ASEKHARAN): (a) and (b) Specific studies to assess the impact of the developmental 
activities on the distribution of benefits across the economic ladder are not available from 
official sources. However, developmental activities in the country are reviewed in each Five 
Year Plans and in the Mid-Term Appraisal of the five Year Plans. The Eleventh Five year 
Plan, which covers the period 2007-08 to 2011 -12, has set the growth target for the economy 
at 9% per year for the Plan period and aims at putting the economy on a sustainable growth 
trajectory with a growth of approximately 10% by the end of its period. Associated with this 
projection involves doubling the growth rate of agriculture to 4% per year compared 2.3% 
per year in the Tenth Plan, raising the industrial growth from 9.2% in the Tenth Plan to 
between 10% and 11% in the Eleventh Plan, and the growth of services sector from 9.3% in 
the Tenth Plan to between 9% and 11% in the Eleventh Plan. The per capita income, measures 
by Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is projected to grow at about 7.6 percent per year to 
double in the less than ten years. Recognizing good qualtiy infrastructure as the most critical 

Written Answers to [13 MARCH 2008] Unstarred Questions    145 
physical requirement for attaining faster growth in a competitive world, the Eleventh Plan 
lays special emphasis for infrastructure deve lopment. The total investment needed in 
infrastructure, defined to include electric power, roads, railways, ports, airports, 
telecommunications, irrigation, drinking water, sanitation, storage and warehousing is 
projected to increase to almost 9% of GDP by the terminal year of the Eleventh Plan. There 
is no projection as to the status of the economy in 2020 AD.

THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS (SHRI 
T.R. BAALl/): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Keeping in view the business dynamics and availability 
of qualified and competent manpower, the shipping companies all over world including

Union of Seafarers of India (NUSI) and Forward Seamen's Union of India (FSUI) along 
with SCI Officers Association and SCI Staff Union Jointly opposed the notice issued by SCI 
inviting tenders for manning and technical management of 30 vessels. The Seafarer's Unions 
apprehend loss of job of the seafarer's as a result of placing the SCI vessels on manning and 
technical management. SCI Officers Association and SCI Staff Union alleged that the jobs 
of clerical/technical nature could not be outsourced under the agreement with the Staff Union. 
They also demanded stopping of the tendering process and convening a meeting with them. 
A reply was sent by SCI to MUI, NUSI, FSUI, SCI Staff Union and the SCI Officers 
Association on February 8,2008 explaining the rationable of the decision and assuring that 
there would be no loss of employment opportunities and the SCI management will completely 
abide by all subsisting agreements and settlements. It was also clarified that a settlement in 
relation to the shore staff that is non-seafaring personnel provided that only the clerical jobs 
which are of perennial nature would not be outsourced and that the contract would not in any 
manner run contrary to the said settlement. The Seafaring Unions were assured that in the 
event of manning and technical management being outsourced, the Seafarer's would continue 
to be employed. The management also had a meeting with the representatives of the Unions 
to address their concern and to assure them th at in the uvent the vessels were outsourced, 
they would be taken into confidence.

National Sea Route and Coastal/Maritime Infrastructure 
1514. SHR1 NAND1 YELLAIAH: Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD 
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) the status of the proposal of the Stat e Government of Andhra Pradesh for 
establishment of National Sea Route and associated coastal/maritime infrastucture along the 
North Coastal districts of Andhra Pradesh with an estimated cost of Rs. 6053 crores; 
(b) the complete details of the proposal; 
(c) the reasons for delay in sanctioning it; 
(d) the response of the Union Government to this proposal; and 
(e) by when it is likely to be given clearance? 
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI T.R. BAALU): (a) to (e) In the context of the exercise undertaken to formulate a 
Policy for the Maritime Sector (Ports, Merchant Shipping and IWT) and the National Maritime 
Development Programme, the Government of Andhra Pradesh submitted a proposal for 
establishment of National Sea waterways along the North Coastal Andhra Pradesh with the 
associated development of Coastal and Marine Infrastructure of Ports/Warehouses and 
complementary development of Coastal and marine Infrastructure and IMO compliances, 
for consideration and approval of the Central Government. The Project component includes 
development and establishment of new ports at 10 locations, development and construction 
of 4 trestle structures, improvements to existing minor ports, logistics nad waterhouses, 
sub-projects like ship-repair facility, fish landing and fishery infrastructure, oil spill response 
unit, ship breaking yard, coastal tourism and recreational infrastructure, sheltered waters 
and ports of refuge as also preparation of Detailed Project Reports. The total project estimate 
as furnished by the government of Andhra Pradsh is Rs. 6053 crores out of which an amount 
of Rs. 1353.60 crores is proposed from private sector and financial support of Rs. 4699 
crores for implementation over a two year programme has been sought from the Central 
Government. 
Under the existing legal framework, the responsibility for development of ports other 
than Major Ports and Shipping & Navigation of Inland Waterways, other than National 
Waterways vests with the respective State Governments, which in this case is Government 
of Andhra Pradesh. Further, there is no scheme under which Central Financial Assistance 
could be rendered for development of the said maritime infrastucture as envisaged by the 
Government of Andhra Pradesh.

levels. Schools will form important component  of PYKKA and will be made the hub of 
sports activities in the panchayats wherever feasible.

Youth Co-ordinators of Nehru Yuvak Kendras 
1551. SHRI PRAVEEN RASHTRAPAL: Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS 
AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) the total number of Youth Co-ordinators of Nehru Yuvak Kendras, State-wise; 
(b) the number of vacancies of Youth Co-ordinators in Nehru Yuvak Kendras 
Department, State-wise; 
(c) when was the last recruitment made in the above cadre; and 
(d) the actions proposed to fill in various vacancies and improve activities of Nehru 
Yuvak Kendras? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI MANI SHANKAR 
AIYAR): (a) and (b) The Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS), has a sanctioned strength 
of 500 Youth Coordinators out of which 165 are lying vacant at present. The Budget proposals 
for 2008-09 have provided for the opening of Nehru Yuva Kendras under a District Youth 
Coordinator in each of the 123 districts of the country not covered at present by NYKS. The 
post of Youth Coordinators are all-India level posts and are liable to be used on an all-India 
basis; hence, the vacancy position is maintained at the national level. 
(c) and (d) The last recruitment of Yout h Coordinators was made in 1994. NYKS 
initiated the process of recruitment of Youth Coordinators in 1996-1997, which was cancelled 
subsequently by the competent authority and later challenged in the Delhi High Court. The 
matter is still-sub-judice. Once the legal issues have been resolved, necessary action will be 
taken to fill up various vacancies. 
A new impetus has been given to the programmes of NYKS by activating the youth 
clubs at the grass-root level. To achieve this, campaigns have been launched in various state/ 
district/block levels to motivate youth clubs to take up activities in the area of social & 
cultural issues, sports and for benefit of the community at the local level. The Panchayat 
Yuva Shakti Abhiyan aimed at synergising the work of youth related to Panchayati Raj 
Institutions and youth working in youth clubs  and mahila mandals is another significant 
innovation of recent origin. The recently approved Panchayat Yuva Krida aur Khel Abhiyan, 
in which the NYKS has major organi sation responsibilities, will give a further fillip to 
energizing NYKS. The programmes of NYKS will further be reviewed on the basis of the 
holistic Management Study conducted by IIM Ahmedabad which is expected to be submitted 
to the Ministry shortly.

SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Sir, I will read out from the Statement of Objects and Reasons 
of the Land Acquisition (Amendment) Bill, 2007 which is pending before the Parliament. It 
says, "The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (the Act) has been an effective instrument for the 
acquisition of land for public purposes and also for companies. Yet, its provisions have been 
found to be inadequate in addressing certain issues relating to the excercise of the statutory 
powers of the State for involuntary acquisition of private land and property. 
Often, such acquisition of land leads to di splacement of people, depriving them of 
their livelihood and shelter, restricting access to their traditional resource base, and uprooting 
them from their spcio-cultural environment. These have traumatic, psychological and socio-
cultural consequences for the affected population, which call for protecting their rights, 
including those of the weaker sections of so ciety, particularly, tribals, tenants, etc. 
Rehabilitation and resettlement of the persons and families affected by involuntary acquisition 
of private and immovable property is of pa ramount importance. Thus, it is necessary to 
extend the provisions of the extant policies or statutes for rehabilitation and resettlement of 
those affected by the acquisition of land under the Act. 
Also, the ambit of the expression "person interested" under the Act is proposed to be 
expanded so as to include tribals and other traditional forest dwellers, who have lost any 
traditional rights recognised under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers 
(Recognitions of Forest Rights) Act, 2006. Moreover, it is necessary to ensure that persons 
having tenancy rights under the relevant State laws are included under the scope of "person 
interested." 
Although the Land Acquisition Act for acquisition of land for public purpose, the 
expression "public purpose" has not been defined. Hence, the necessity of defining "public 
purpose," so as to restrict the scope of land acquisition under the Act to provision of land for 
strategic purposes vital to the State, and for infrastructure projects where the benefits accrue 
to the general public is essential. 

206   Government [RAJYASABHA] Bills 
The provisions of the Act are also used to acquire private lands for companies. This 
frequently raises a question mark on the desirability of such State intervention when land 
could be arranged by the company through private negotiations on a "willing-seller and 
willing-buyer" basis, which could be seen to be a more fair arrangement from the point of 
view of the land owner. In view of this, it is desirable to omit the provisions for ^acquisition 
of land for companies under the Act. However, under certain circumstances; it may be 
necessary to acquire some land through statutory mechanism to the extent of a limited portion 
of the total area of the land required when the "person" has already purchased the rest of the 
land through private negotiations and the purpose is useful to the general public. Such "person" 
may include any company or association or body of individuals, whether incorporated or 
not." 
Sir, the point is, they have deliberated on the issue. And, it is a comprehensive Act 
which is pending before the Parliament. Let this Act be passed first. Let the Land Acquisition 
Act, 1894 be amended. For example, in Singur, why did the problem arise there? Sir, the 
tenants of the land; those who were the tillers, they were given land to plough the land, but, 
they were not allowed to get the compensation. 
SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT: What are you talking? ...(Interruptions)... 
SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Let me complete. The point is, the original patta holders, 
they create problem. The tiller does not get the compensation. The same thing will happen 
here. Those who are tenants of the land for 50 years or 100 years are ploughing the land and 
the zamindar is staying in Bombay, Kolkata or Delhi. So, they should get compensation. 
That provision is coming through this Bill, Sir. This Bill is under the consideration of the 
Standing Committee. Let the Report come. Thereafter, the hon. Minister can come and discuss 
the matter. What is the hurry? There is no hurry in passing this Bill. So, my submission, Sir, 
is that please consider this. It should be sent to the Select Committee of Rajya Sabha which 
can take up this matter. Let it be discussed there. Sir, I move a Motion to send it to the Select 
Committee. Let there be Members from all political parties in that Committee. Don't snatch 
the right of the poor people who are having small land holdings thought this notification. He 
will not get the due compensation. He will not get any employment. He has been earning his 
bread and butter right from his forefathers' time. He will not get anything. Where will he be 
resettled? As Laluji says, it looks very simple, but it wi11 have very far-reaching consequences. 
Not only will it break the heart, it will also break the federal structure of our country. It will 
also kill those farmers who are earning their bread and butter out of it. So, this is not fair, Sir. 
Let the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, which is very comprehensive, be passed. Thereafter, 
they should bring all these things. Till that time, this matter should be referred to the Select 
Committee of Rajya Sabha. Let Shrimati Brinda Karat head that Committee. Thank you.

DR. E.M. SUDARSANA NATCHIAPPAN (Tamil Nadu): Sir, I support the Food Safety 
and Standards (Amendment) Bill, 2008. Actually, the purpose is very much restricted to 
accommodate certain persons who have got expertise in this field. The Chairperson of the 
Food Authority can be a part-time Member. The age-limit is also 65 years. Nowadays, many 
bureaucrats, after retirement, get jobs, so that their experience can be used in these types of 
authorities. 
In the modern world, the food safety and standards are very important. When we are 
having a global competition, our food material should be of an international standard. Even 
though we are having many laws to prevent substandard type of food being sold we are very 
poor in maintaining the standards. This particular Authority has to come forward with proper 
regulations, so that our fixed standards for food material are maintained properly. 
The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act got certain provisions. But, in many cases, it 
has not fulfilled the obligations. The State Government Authorities are using that Act very 
rarely and that too for statistical purpose. They are catching hold of certain poor people who 
are selling them, like vendors or shopkeepers. But, the persons, who are producing in the 
brand name or even in the fake name, are le ft scot-free. For any food material, even for 
drinking water, nowadays, it is very easy to pack up in a particular known brand name and 
put the water or any soft drink or any food material and the packet will be standing in some 
other name. It is sold in that particular name and at that particular price. There is no strict 
prohibition or enforcement of this Act. During the 20-Point Programme implementation 
Madam Indira Gandhiji was the Prime Minister. She could have made this programme proper 
by enforcing throughout India. At that time, there was Emergency also. Therefore, the officials 
were also working properly and it was enforced properly. Nowadays, there is nothing like 
that and many people are getting disease only because of this type of foods which are not 
properly standardised or they are shown as if they are properly standardised. Sir, it is very 
surprising to note that even drinking water is sold for Rs. 15 per bottle. But, when the milk 
prices were raised to Rs. 15 per litre, there was agitation. Poor widows and agriculturists 
depend on milk. We used to say that "you add water into milk." Nowadays, "if you add 
water, it is much more costlier than the milk." That is the situation now which we are facing. 
It becomes a habit. 
Now, the middle class people, and even the lower middle class people, carry mineral 
water. Standard is fixed for mineral water. But, there is no enforcement. Anybody can take 
his own pipe water, put it in a brand bottle and sell it off just by putting a plastic cover 
around it. They are also putting a type of paper on it to make the people believe. In urgent 
situations, people purchase water bottles. Anywhere, we can purchase drinking water or any 
material which is in the brand name. Sir, It's high time. We are making a lot of laws, but, we 
are not enforcing them properly. The burden is shifting on to the consumer. The basic law is 

Government [13 MARCH 2008] Bills   213 
'beware' or 'consumer should be beware'. That is the law. But, at the same time, materials are 
flooded into the market. When the materials are flooded into the market, our Government 
should regulate it properly. If an industry is involved in fake production, then, it has to be 
sealed and it has to be exposed to the public saying that these are the people who are making 
fake things. We were surprised to know that fake notes are coming from Malaysia, Sri Lanka, 
etc. From all around, our neighbours are bringing fake Indian rupee notes into the Indian 
market. That is the situation we are facing. But, food materials have got much more bad 
effect. It affects the ordinary people, especially babies who take this type of substandard 
materials. They are suffering and they are dying. In the same way, ordinary people are now 
wooed by market and advertisements and they purchase it. We can take one example of coca 
cola. Coca cola is in a brand bottle. We can get any type of coca cola in villages. Beverages 
have an age limit, saying that beyond a particul ar age, chemicals cannot subsist. But, in 
villages, one-month old or one-year old coca cola is also sold. What is the action that we are 
taking? Therefore, in one way, we are prescribing the standards, we are making the laws, we 
are making dynamic organisations, but, at the same time, it is important to note whether we 
are enforcing them properly or not. Sir, for this, we need a better coordination among all the 
three layers of the Government—the Central Government, the State Governments and the 
Panchayat Governments. All the three have to make it and the things which are now available 
in mass production in a brand name, it reaches the villages. Brand publicity is also given, 
but, the thing inside is—as we used to call it—"Old wine in new bottle". Old wine is not 
available, but substandard material is in the new bottle. That is the brand name. Therefore, I 
request, when the Government is thinking of giving more powers to the Authority under the 
Food Safety and Standards Act, that the Chairperson to whom particularly these powers are 
being given, who has to be a full-time Chairperson, has to look after all these things. Now, 
this Bill allows even people from companies which are producing food materials to be 
Members of this particular body. This Bill indirectly provides for that. Therefore, they will 
come and try to be Members of the body compet itively so that they can do their business 
according to their own terms. They can manipulate things. They can make their officials to 
be the implementing authorities and control them because they are Members of the body. It 
is better not to accommodate persons who are doing business in this body. Persons who have 
expertise, who have scientific knowledge and sympathy towards the people should be 
appointed as Members and Chairperson. They should implement the law properly because it 
tells upon the life of millions of people. When it is standardised, they believe in the brand 
mark and take that it is a standardised food. Therefore, the standards should be properly 
fixed. Therefore, I request the Government to take serious action, if there is any violation of 
this particular law. Thank you.

growth. Secondly, equal opportunities must be created for all, through a level-playing field.

for which they are not responsible. In the end, I would like say that a Fifteen Point-Programme 
is given by our Prime Minister. For that, I think, from the Budget, the minorities may not get 
the benefit. So, I request the hon. Finance Minister that minority component Plan, a separate 
Plan, should be constituted so that from the Budget the minorities can get benefit. Finally, I 
fervently hope that the hon, Finance Minister's belief that the best is yet to come for India is 
borne out in future. So, I thank heartily the hon. Finance Minister, under the guidance of our 
hon. Prime Minister and our Chairperson, Shrimati Soniaji. He has given an excellent Budget 
which will surely improve the development of India.

 SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN (Kerala): Sir, we are discussing the annual Budget of 
this year, which deals with the problems of more than 100 million people. This country has 
great expectations from this Government this year since we are faci ng an acute crisis in 
agriculture as well as a hike in the prices of essential commodities. Sir, the poor people are 
becoming the victims of this situation. Ours is an agrarian country where still 65 per cent 
people earn their livelihood by means of agriculture. We are facing a deep crisis. On the one 
side, suicides by the farmers and deaths of the poor people are being reported; on the other 
side, we are facing a fall in the production and productivity. Sir, naturally, this Budget should 
address both these questions, but unfortunately, only one issue has been addressed, that is, 
the debt trap in which our farmers have fallen. Sir, every year, millions of farmers in this 
country are losing their farming land. That is  the problem. Because of the hike in the 
investment in agriculture, the poor farmer is not in a position to make that much of investment. 
Every year, agriculture is proving to be a loss- making business for small farmers. So, naturally, 
they have to go in for loans. Whatever price he is getting for the produce is lesser than his 
expectation, Naturally, after four or five years of failure in agriculture, he is forced to sell off 
his land and thus, becomes a landless farmer. That is why the number of agricultural workers 
is increasing and migration is also increasing. This issue has to be addressed properly. In 
this Budget, only one part has been addressed, that is, the debt relief. I welcome this. But the 
other part still remains to be addressed. Sir, the allocation for agriculture should be enhanced. 
Other infrastructure should also be made available, Whatever is already there is not sufficient. 
Unless we improve the quality of agriculture by improving the productivity, we will not be 
in a position to address this problem. Sir, the Budget has, unfortunately, failed to address 
this very important question. And, while we are failing in addressing this issue, we will fail 
in two areas. Sir, for the first time in this country, we are facing the problem of price hike of 
the essential commodities because of the failure of production of foodgrains. Sir, for the 
first time, we don't have sufficient paddy, we don't have sufficient wheat, and we don't have 
sufficient cereals. So, in such a situation, the Government has to enhance its investment in
